title: iter-4 bit-127 mask is unreachable from any test (formula correct in code, unverified by suite)
description: Iter-4 fixed the iter-3 critical: the price decode now masks bit 127 before the >>64 shift, so asks no longer return ~9.22e18. Per synthesis-notes the formula is empirically verified against captured order_ids (bid 12377783720203182843884075 -> 671000, ask 170141183460486719245069180370816077150 -> 948000). However the iter-3 'zero tests exercise this code' half is unchanged: T-014's suix_getDynamicFields stub returns {data: [], hasNextPage: false} (networkShape.test.ts:115), so traverseBigVector returns [] at line 168 before entering the slice loop. The entire block at lines 196-253 — including the new ASK_FLAG_MASK constant, the masked >>64 decode, the Number.isFinite branch, and the Order.price assignment — is unreachable from any of the 24 tests. A regression that flipped the mask to (1n<<128n)-1n (no-op), removed the mask entirely (reverting to iter-3's broken state), or zeroed the price field would ship green.
impact: AC1.4 (correct mid-price) now relies on a code path that exists in production but is exercised by zero assertions. The fix is real but the regression-resistance the test suite is supposed to provide does not extend to it. A future refactor that touches this block has no executable safety net.
recommendation: Tests are sealed for this cycle. Next cycle: extend T-014's spy so that for objectId === '0xfakeasks' the suix_getDynamicFields response returns one slice, and the follow-up sui_getObject for that slice returns a Slice<Order> with one entry whose order_id is the captured ask 170141183460486719245069180370816077150 string. Then assert the runDataLayer return value's first PoolCardData has midPrice/bestAsk consistent with 948000 (not 9.22e18 and not undefined).

title: iter-4 console.warn no longer silent — but no test asserts the warning fires
description: Iter-4 addressed the iter-3 silent-swallow concern: the BigInt try/catch now console.warn's both on parse failure and on non-finite Number coercion, with the malformed order_id and error message in the payload. This is a real improvement at runtime — a corrupted on-chain order_id will now appear in the browser console. The remaining test-vs-impl gap is small: T-018 (App.test.tsx:96-130) spies on console.error and asserts zero calls, but no test spies on console.warn. So the warning could be silently removed in a future refactor and no test would fail. This is an order of magnitude smaller than the iter-3 finding (silent swallow → silent loss of injection); demoted to low because the production behavior is now correct and only the test-side observation hook is missing.
impact: Future refactor that drops the warn() calls reverts to silent fallback without breaking any test. Diagnostic regression risk only — no functional regression risk in iter-4 itself.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Next cycle: extend the dataLayer integration test (the same one suggested in R5-001) to include a deliberately malformed order_id ('not-a-number') and assert that console.warn was called with /dataLayer.*BigInt|order_id/.

title: marketStats T-005..T-008 fixtures still construct Orders without `price` — compute-side ternary's left arm exercised by zero assertions
description: Iter-4 did not change marketStats.ts's compute-side branch: `o.price !== undefined ? o.price : decodeAskPrice(o.order_id)` (lines 49 and 55). The order(...) helper at marketStats.test.ts:52-64 still returns `{order_id, quantity, filled_quantity, status}` with no price field, so the ternary's left arm (the production-preferred path) is never taken in any of T-005..T-008. A bug that swapped the ternary to `o.price !== undefined ? decodeAskPrice(o.order_id) : o.price` (nonsense in production: ignores injected price, returns undefined for injection-less fixtures) would still pass T-005..T-008 — the fixture path always lands on decode anyway. Carry-forward from iter-3 R5-003. Iter-4's bit-127 mask actually makes this gap more salient: the production data layer now reliably injects bit-127-masked prices, but the compute layer's preference for that injection over its own decoders is verified by no assertion.
impact: AC1.4: the 'data layer injects price → compute layer prefers it' contract is verified by zero assertions end-to-end. R5-001 (data-layer side) and this finding (compute-layer side) together mean the full design is unverified at every layer.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Next cycle: add one fixture row to T-005 where order(...) accepts an optional `price` parameter and the assertion is `expect(stats.bestAsk).toBe(<injectedPrice>)` regardless of what decodeAskPrice would have returned (e.g. set order_id so its mask-decode yields 9999 but inject price=1010, then assert bestAsk===1010).

title: iter-4 buildDeps() factory in main.tsx exercised by zero tests
description: Iter-4 refactored main.tsx: the iter-2/iter-3 `let cachedPackageId; deps.loadManifest = …` pattern was replaced with a buildDeps() factory that captures packageId in a shared closure between loadManifest and fetchPoolStats. The refactor is structurally clean (no module-level mutable state) and adds a defensive guard at lines 55-60 that throws if fetchPoolStats is called before loadManifest resolves. None of these new behaviors is covered by any test. App.test.tsx injects AppDeps directly via props (line 64-77, 105-120 etc.) and never imports main.tsx. So: a regression that swapped the order of `packageId = manifest.deepbookPackageId` and `return manifest`, removed the await before fetch(MANIFEST_URL), changed MANIFEST_URL to a wrong path, dropped the parseManifest call, removed the createRoot mount, or accidentally returned an object literal that captures `packageId` by value at construction time (a closure-by-value mistake) — all would ship green.
impact: AC1.1 (manifest fetch) and AC1.2 (per-pool stats wiring) integration glue is unverified. The new defensive throw at lines 55-60 is also untestable from the suite, so a future refactor that removes the guard re-introduces the iter-2 race silently.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Next cycle: export buildDeps() from main.tsx and add a unit test that (a) stubs globalThis.fetch to return a fixture manifest body, (b) calls deps.loadManifest(), (c) calls deps.fetchPoolStats(descriptor) and asserts it does not throw the 'wiring bug' error, (d) constructs deps then calls fetchPoolStats BEFORE loadManifest and asserts the wiring-bug error fires. Keep main.tsx's createRoot mount line outside the export so the test does not pull react-dom.

title: 30s sparkline refresh still untested (carry-forward from iter-3 R5-005 / iter-2 R5-004)
description: Iter-4 did not touch App.tsx. The setInterval(REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=20_000) polling effect at lines 91-125 remains uncovered. No test uses vi.useFakeTimers() or asserts deps.fetchPoolStats is called more than once after mount. The interval runs only when state.status === 'ready' (early-return at line 92), so a bug that left state in 'loading' would silently disable polling forever, and the cleanup at line 124 (clearInterval) is also unverified — a leaked interval would only manifest under jsdom teardown noise.
impact: AC1.3 (freshness within 30s) has zero executable enforcement. A wrong interval value, missing useEffect dep, swapped state check, or missed cleanup leak ships green.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Next cycle: add a test using vi.useFakeTimers(), advance clock by 25s, assert deps.fetchPoolStats has been called 2x (once on mount + once on interval). For cleanup verification, render then unmount, advance 25s, assert no further fetchPoolStats calls.

title: Vite dev-server middleware still untested (carry-forward from iter-3 R5-006 / iter-2 R5-011)
description: Iter-4 did not address this. The Vite middleware that bridges browser-to-localnet.json reads from a hardcoded `~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/deployments/localnet.json` path and has zero tests. A regression in vite.config.ts (wrong path, broken middleware ordering, accidental removal during a config refactor) only surfaces when a developer runs pnpm dev — never in CI.
impact: Same as iter-2/iter-3. The dev-only bridge between dev server and SPA is not subject to the per-cycle red/green gate.
recommendation: Add a vitest spec that imports the config and verifies the middleware function shape (registers a handler for /localnet.json, reads from MANIFEST_DISK_PATH, returns 404 with the deploy-all hint on ENOENT), OR document explicitly that this is dev-only out-of-gate.

title: T-014 spy still returns identical canned response for all sui_getObject calls — iter-4 traversal branch and bit-127 decode both unexercised
description: Iter-4 did not change T-014. The spy returns the same 'leaf' PoolInner payload for every sui_getObject call (lines 82-113), so resolvePoolInnerFields hits the early-return `if ('book' in fields) return fields` at dataLayer.ts:117 every time. The Pool→Versioned→getDynamicFields→PoolInner-field-wrapper branch (dataLayer.ts:119-152) — production's actual shape per chain-shape.md — is exercised by zero tests. Combined with R5-001, this means iter-4's bit-127-masked decode (the entire reason iter-4 exists) is unexercised at every layer: traversal never reaches BigVector slices because suix_getDynamicFields returns empty, and the Versioned→PoolInner traversal never runs because the spy collapses the chain to a leaf.
impact: AC1.5 ('no indexer call') is verified, but the chain-direct production shape correctness is not. T-014's name 'outbound HTTP shape lockdown' is honest; it does NOT verify production traversal correctness or price-decode correctness.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Next cycle: add a separate test for traversal correctness with a captured real-shape fixture — the spy keys on objectId, not just method name, returning Pool wrapper for the pool object, getDynamicFields with a real wrapper field id, the wrapper field with value.fields.book wiring, and a non-empty BigVector traversal that ends in a Slice<Order> with the captured ask order_id 170141183460486719245069180370816077150. Assert midPrice ≈ 948000.

title: types.ts Order.price docstring still describes event-payload provenance; iter-4 actually decodes from order_id (bit-127 masked)
description: Order.price's docstring at types.ts:60-74 says 'price is NOT on the chain Order struct; it is injected by the data layer from the corresponding OrderInfo event payload to avoid order_id bit-decode errors on bid orders'. Iter-4's actual implementation (dataLayer.ts:204-245) injects price by bit-decoding the order_id with the bit-127 mask — the exact thing the doc says it is avoiding. Iter-4's empirical verification in synthesis-notes shows the masked bit-decode is correct against the captured ask AND bid (671000 and 948000), so the docstring's premise ('to avoid order_id bit-decode errors on bid orders') is now stale — the bit-decode is correct on bids too, given the mask. No test asserts the provenance, so this drift is invisible to the test gate.
impact: Low at the test-gate layer (no test cares about doc-comments) but feeds into reader-confusion: someone trusting the doc-comment will look for an event-payload wiring that does not exist. They may try to 'fix' the absent wiring and break the working bit-decode.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Update the docstring (no test impact) to reflect iter-4 reality: 'injected by the data layer via bit-127-masked decode of order_id high 64 bits; see dataLayer.ts traverseBigVector for the empirical verification against captured order_ids in chain-shape.md'.
evidence:
/**
 * Order struct shape from Slice<Order> content — see chain-shape.md Step 4.
 *
 * `price` is NOT on the chain Order struct; it is injected by the data layer
 * from the corresponding OrderInfo event payload to avoid order_id bit-decode
 * errors on bid orders (see chain-shape.md "Critical decoding note").
 */

title: iter-4 ASK_FLAG_MASK literal duplicates marketStats.ts's ASK_BIT_OFFSET — drift risk with no test invariant
description: Iter-4 introduced `const ASK_FLAG_MASK = (1n << 127n) - 1n;` inline inside traverseBigVector's per-order loop (dataLayer.ts:220). The same magic number lives in marketStats.ts:22 as `const ASK_BIT_OFFSET = 1n << 127n;` (used as `id & (ASK_BIT_OFFSET - 1n)` in decodeAskPrice). Two separate constants describing the same bit layout with no shared source of truth. No test asserts they agree; a future refactor that bumps marketStats.ts's encoding (e.g. moves the ask flag to bit 126) would silently desync from dataLayer.ts. This is a correctness landmine hidden inside a tests-vs-impl gap: the tests can't notice because the dataLayer's masked-decode block is unreachable per R5-001 and R5-007.
impact: Low today (both constants describe the same encoding correctly per chain-shape.md) but the lack of any shared source plus the unreachability of the data-layer code path means a future encoding change has zero gate enforcement on agreement.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Next cycle: extract `ASK_BIT_OFFSET` and the masked-decode helper to a shared `src/orderIdCodec.ts` module, import from both dataLayer and marketStats, add a unit test that asserts the codec round-trips a captured ask order_id to its captured price.
